title: CS4421 — Containerization Engineering & Container Ecosystem
description: Practice test covering Docker containerization theory, multi-stage builds, the 12-Factor App methodology, layer caching, container observability, and Amazon ECR deployments.

questions.prompt: Which of the following mechanisms provide the underlying isolation for lightweight containers running on a shared Linux host?

options.text: Hypervisor virtualization
Full Guest OS allocation
Namespaces and Cgroups
Enterprise Orchestration

questions.explanation: Containers utilize the shared host Linux kernel and are isolated using Linux Namespaces and Cgroups, unlike Virtual Machines which rely on a hypervisor and full Guest OS.

questions.prompt: According to the 12-Factor App methodology covered in the material, which of the following practices should a containerized application follow?

options.text: Ensure fast startup and clean shutdown upon receiving SIGTERM signals.
Maintain strict separation of config from code by passing variables at runtime.
Store configuration and secrets directly inside the immutable container image code.
Treat processes as stateless, meaning container instances share nothing.

questions.explanation: The 12-Factor App methodology dictates Disposability (fast startup/clean shutdown), Config in Environment (passing variables at runtime), and Stateless Processes. Storing config in code violates the first tenet.

questions.prompt: When preparing your repository for containerization, which specific directories are explicitly recommended to be placed in the `.dockerignore` file?

options.text: dist/
node_modules/
server/
.git/
src/

questions.explanation: The lab materials specifically instruct the creation of a .dockerignore file to prevent copying the local 'node_modules/' and '.git/' directories into the container image.

questions.prompt: A developer writes the following Dockerfile snippet. According to best practices for layer caching optimization, what is the primary issue with this approach?
questions.codeSnippet:
COPY . .
RUN npm install
RUN npm run build

options.text: npm install requires a builder stage to execute successfully on Alpine Linux.
It copies the entire codebase before installing dependencies, meaning npm install will unnecessarily run on every single code change.
The layers are cached efficiently, but npm run build should precede npm install.
It relies on Docker Compose to bind ports before the build finishes.

questions.explanation: Because 'COPY . .' invalidates the layer cache whenever any file in the repository changes, the slow 'npm install' step will execute on every build, severely degrading performance.

questions.prompt: Match the tool to its correct category or role in the container ecosystem. Which of the following statements are true based on the provided material?

options.text: AWS App Runner acts as a managed Cloud PaaS for executing serverless containers.
Docker Compose is an enterprise orchestration tool designed for auto-scaling multi-node clusters.
Kubernetes provides enterprise orchestration for massive distributed microservice architectures.
Podman is a runtime engine used to build and execute isolated containers on a host.

questions.explanation: Docker Compose is strictly for local orchestration of multi-container stacks, not enterprise auto-scaling. Kubernetes, AWS App Runner, and Podman are correctly described.

questions.prompt: You need to diagnose a running container named "my-blog". Which commands are specifically used for inspecting the live container health check status or monitoring live CPU/RAM usage?

options.text: docker build --platform linux/amd64 -t my-blog:latest
docker tag my-blog:latest <ecr_uri>/my-blog:latest
docker inspect --format='{{json .State.Health}}' my-blog | jq
docker stats
docker logs -f my-blog

questions.explanation: 'docker inspect' can be formatted to view the health check status, and 'docker stats' provides live CPU/RAM usage meters.

questions.prompt: Which of the following commands correctly runs a container locally in detached mode while injecting a production environment variable and mapping host port 4321 to container port 4321?

options.text: docker run -d -p 80:4321 -e NODE_ENV=development --name my-blog astro-blog:v1.0.0
docker build -d -p 4321:4321 --platform linux/amd64 astro-blog:v1.0.0
docker run -d -p 4321:4321 -e NODE_ENV=production --name my-blog astro-blog:v1.0.0
aws ecr get-login-password | docker run -p 4321:4321 astro-blog:v1.0.0

questions.explanation: The correct command uses 'run' with '-d' for detached mode, '-p 4321:4321' for port mapping, and '-e NODE_ENV=production' for the environment variable injection.

questions.prompt: What is the primary architectural purpose of separating a multi-stage Dockerfile into a "builder" stage and a "runner" stage?

options.text: To compile the application in a heavy environment and then copy only the necessary artifacts to a lean production runner, reducing the final image size.
To automatically orchestrate the container across multiple nodes using Kubernetes.
To allow the host hypervisor to allocate a full Guest OS exclusively for the runner stage.
To push the code to Amazon ECR before the final runner stage begins execution.

questions.explanation: Multi-stage builds allow developers to use a feature-rich builder image to compile code, and then extract only the finished artifacts into a separate, lean runner image, vastly reducing the attack surface and final image size.

questions.prompt: Review the following multi-stage Dockerfile snippet. Based on the 12-Factor App methodology and layer caching principles from the material, which statements are accurate?
questions.codeSnippet:
FROM node:20-alpine AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY . .
RUN npm run build

FROM node:20-alpine AS runner
WORKDIR /app
ENV NODE_ENV=production HOST=0.0.0.0 PORT=4321
COPY --from=builder /app/package.json ./
COPY --from=builder /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY --from=builder /app/dist ./dist
EXPOSE 4321
CMD ["node", "./dist/server/entry.mjs"]

options.text: By injecting ENV HOST=0.0.0.0 PORT=4321, the configuration satisfies the 12-Factor App tenet for Port Binding.
The runner stage will crash because it does not re-run npm ci to install dependencies.
The container relies on a shared hypervisor initialized exclusively in the runner stage.
The package.json copy in the builder stage successfully leverages Docker layer caching to skip npm ci unless dependency files change.

questions.explanation: Copying package.json before the rest of the source code ensures layer caching isolates 'npm ci'. Binding to 0.0.0.0 satisfies the Port Binding tenet. The runner does not need to run npm ci because it copies the node_modules folder directly from the builder stage.

questions.prompt: Before you can successfully execute `docker push <ecr_uri>/astro-blog:v1.0.0` to deploy your image to Amazon Elastic Container Registry, what exact sequence of preliminary steps must you perform according to the lab architecture?

options.text: Execute docker logs -f to verify the local container health, then run aws ecr get-login-password.
Authenticate the Docker CLI to Amazon ECR using aws ecr get-login-password, then use docker tag to associate the ECR URI with your local image.
Run docker compose up to authenticate with AWS, then execute docker tag.
Create a .dockerignore file with the ECR URI to bypass local orchestration constraints.

questions.explanation: You must pipe the AWS CLI authentication token into 'docker login' to authorize the client, and then 'docker tag' the local image with the remote ECR URI before pushing.
